title: design: autophage owns the pull request it opened, through review to merge
description: Today a case ends the moment the PR opens: RecordOutcome moves it to Done on pull_request_opened, and CaseState.Terminal() covers Done, so nothing that happens on the PR afterwards can reach the case. Case.Close already refuses on a terminal case, which is why merging PR #3 landed as deliveries_total{result="rejected"}. Owning the PR means Done stops being terminal, or a state follows it. The App is subscribed to issues, installation and installation_repositories only, so review events do not arrive at all: pull_request_review carries the approval, pull_request_review_comment and issue_comment carry the feedback.
design: New facts and vocabulary: a review-feedback fact, a revise attempt kind that starts from the case branch instead of repo.DefaultBranch, and outcome kinds for revised and merged, since pull_request_opened is the only success today. Trust: an approval has to mean a pull_request_review with state APPROVED from a login with write access, which is a different question from the issue-author association the gate uses now, and merging is a write capability the App has but has never used. Loop safety: autophage pushes, a comment arrives, autophage pushes again, so the budget has to span the revision series rather than one attempt, and the existing BotLogin check in translate.go must keep it from answering itself. Shares almost everything with autophage-07h: both subscribe to pull request events and both work an existing branch, so the dependabot path becomes a caller of this context rather than a second implementation. Build this one first.
acceptance_criteria: A PR autophage opened is revised from review comments and merged on approval, without a human driving any step, and without the case being able to loop on its own comments.
notes: Build-this-one-first no longer holds for the dependabot path. ADR 0007 makes Upkeep a separate context: a Bump is not a Case (five Resolution terms mean something different or nothing at all), so the dependabot work does not wait on this. What they still genuinely share is the pull_request subscription and pushing to a branch autophage did not cut, and Upkeep lands both first (autophage-d9r, autophage-n4o) so this issue inherits them rather than the other way round. The green-is-not-terminal lesson from autophage-2lq is already applied in the Bump state machine and should be applied here too.

title: autophage v1: watcher that fixes GitHub issues in a sandboxed agent
description: Design: docs/specs/2026-09-04-autophage-design.md, domain model, contracts, ADRs 0001 to 0006. Five plans under docs/plans/.

title: upkeep: agent repair runner
description: internal/agent gains the repair pipeline: mint a token, PrepareHead at the failing sha, start the container, dial the toolbox, run the budgeted agent on the failing check output, CommitAndPush onto dependabot's branch, map every step's failure to a RepairOutcome. Mirrors Runner.execute for cases, minus OpenPullRequest: a repair pushes and stops, because the bump's success is green checks, not a pull request.
design: Split out of autophage-a51, which now covers the app services alone. Runner.execute is 270 case-shaped lines; the repair pipeline reuses the same sandbox and agent ports with PrepareHead instead of Prepare and no pull request step. Worth looking at what the two can genuinely share before duplicating the step-to-outcome mapping, since near-identical functions are exactly what the self-review rule is about.
acceptance_criteria: A red bump reaches the agent, the agent commits a fix, the push lands on dependabot's branch and the bump returns to awaiting_checks on the new head.
close_reason: internal/agent/repair.go: the Repairer. Seven tests green against real Postgres, and the daemon now wires RepairScheduler and RepairCanceller when upkeep.enabled is set.

title: make check is green while every Postgres test skips
description: internal/storetest skips when Docker is unreachable and AUTOPHAGE_TEST_DSN is unset. On this Mac Docker is not running, so make check passes having run zero store, app and storetest database tests. Found while landing autophage-br4: the full suite only actually ran once AUTOPHAGE_TEST_DSN was pointed at the local Homebrew postgres@18, and it then caught a stale table-count tripwire (34 vs 54) that make check had been reporting as green.
design: The skip is right for a contributor with no Docker and wrong for the gate. Options: make check exports a DSN when one is reachable and fails otherwise; a make target that starts the container explicitly; or storetest fails rather than skips when an env var marks the run as the gate. Also note two packages sharing one DSN interfere, since each Truncates in cleanup while others run: go test ./... needs -p 1 against a shared server, or a database per package.
acceptance_criteria: A skipped database test cannot leave make check green.

title: upkeep: RepairScheduler, RepairRunner, StaleCheckSweeper and recovery
description: internal/app gains the Upkeep half of the loop. RepairScheduler (domain service): queued bumps start FIFO by their transition into queued; no round for a repository without a watch row or removed from the installation; no round past the cap. RepairRunner: PrepareHead, run the agent on the failing contexts and the diff, CommitAndPush, record the outcome. StaleCheckSweeper: abandon an awaiting_checks bump whose wait window elapsed, reason checks_never_concluded. Recovery: an open round at boot ends Aborted{DaemonRestart}, or Aborted{PullRequestClosed} when the bump is already closed.
design: The shared concurrency limit is not a domain rule of either context: at most sandbox.concurrency agent runs exist across issue attempts and repair rounds together, because there is one sandbox pool. That belongs to the Dispatcher, an application service arbitrating a shared resource. Nothing currently prioritises between the two, which ADR 0007 records as the operational risk and which this issue does not solve.
acceptance_criteria: A red bump reaches a repair round, pushes, and the new head starts a fresh wait window; the round cap stops the third round; an infra failure requeues and a model failure abandons.
close_reason: RepairScheduler, StaleCheckSweeper, BumpRecovery and BuildRepairBrief landed, with the upkeep config section and daemon wiring. Concurrency is now shared: both schedulers subtract open issue attempts and open repair rounds, since there is one sandbox pool. RepairScheduler is left unwired in the daemon until autophage-am9 lands the agent repair runner.

title: upkeep: GitHub boundary for pull_request, check_suite and workflow_run
description: internal/github gains: translation of pull_request (opened, reopened, synchronize, closed), check_suite.completed and workflow_run.completed into Bump commands; GetPullRequest; CheckRollup. Contracts in docs/specs/2026-09-17-autophage-upkeep-contracts.md under Internal ports. The App must also subscribe to the three events (runbook step 4 lists only issues, installation, installation_repositories).
design: A single check_suite.completed does not mean the checks are done: a head can have several suites and nothing in the payload says how many. So the adapter queries the combined rollup for the sha and records a verdict only when no run is still queued or in progress. GitHub's eight conclusions collapse onto our two: success, skipped and neutral are success; failure, timed_out and action_required are failure; cancelled and stale leave it inconclusive and record nothing. A bump is only created when the PR author is the dependabot login AND an upkeep_watches row exists; everything else is an ignored processing row, not a rejection.
acceptance_criteria: Golden-payload tests for each of the five actions, including a check_suite.completed whose rollup is still pending recording no verdict at all.
close_reason: internal/github/bumps.go and rollup.go. pull_request opened/reopened/synchronize/closed, check_suite and workflow_run completions, CheckRollup and GetPullRequest. Runbook now lists the three new subscriptions. 22 new tests green against real Postgres.

title: upkeep: sandbox checkout pinned to a head sha, no rebase
description: internal/sandbox gains PrepareHead(ctx, repository, cloneURL, branch, headSha, token). Fetch, then check out headSha exactly. Workspace.BaseSha and Workspace.RemoteHead are both headSha, so CommitAndPush leases against the head CI judged.
design: The existing checkout always rebases the branch onto the default branch, which is right for a branch autophage cut and wrong for dependabot's: rebasing changes the tree CI just judged, so the round would start from a state no verdict describes. This is also the first time autophage pushes to a branch it did not create; the force-with-lease is what keeps that honest, failing rather than clobbering a dependabot force-push that landed mid-round.
acceptance_criteria: Test against a local bare remote: a repair push onto a branch whose remote head moved under it fails rather than overwriting.
close_reason: PrepareHead landed in internal/sandbox/head.go, on the Sandbox port. Pins the exact head sha, refuses a sha the branch no longer points at, and leases CommitAndPush against it so a dependabot force-push mid-round wins. make check green.

title: upkeep: Bump aggregate, enums and facts
description: New internal/upkeep package: the Bump aggregate root with NewBump, LoadBump, RecordVerdict, AdvanceHead, StartRepair, RecordRun, RecordOutcome, Abandon, Retry, Close, and the value objects CheckVerdict, RepairAttempt, RepairOutcome, BumpAbandonment, BumpClosure, BumpTransition, Watch. Enums: BumpState, CheckConclusion, RepairOutcomeKind, RepairAbortReason, AbandonReason, ClosureKind, BumpTransitionCause. Shapes and rules in docs/specs/2026-09-17-autophage-upkeep-domain-model.md.
design: Mirrors internal/resolution/case.go: unexported fields, constructor-enforced invariants, a Changes struct so the store persists exactly what moved, ErrRefused and ErrInvalid. Budget, Limit, Usage, Run, Brief and FailureClass are imported from internal/resolution as shared kernel, not copied. AbortReason is NOT shared: Upkeep owns RepairAbortReason because issue_closed is invalid here and pull_request_closed is invalid there. green and abandoned are deliberately non-terminal; only closed is, which is the lesson autophage-2lq recorded on the Case side. A failed outcome with class infra requeues, model and agent abandon.
acceptance_criteria: Table-driven tests over every transition in the model state diagram, and a refusal test for every transition it does not draw. A verdict for a stale head sha is refused, not applied.
close_reason: internal/upkeep landed: Bump aggregate, Watch, seven enums, the facts and LoadBump. 88.8% statement coverage, 71 tests, make check green.

title: upkeep: store schema for bumps, verdicts, repair rounds and watches
description: Migration 0002 adding the Upkeep tables and vocabularies from docs/specs/2026-09-17-autophage-upkeep-contracts.md: bump_states, check_conclusions, repair_outcome_kinds, repair_abort_reasons, abandon_reasons, closure_kinds, bump_transition_causes, then upkeep_watches, bumps, bump_transitions, bump_check_verdicts, bump_repairs, bump_repair_runs, bump_repair_outcomes and its four variant tables, bump_abandonments, bump_closures. budget_limits and failure_classes are reused from 0001 (shared kernel). Store methods mirror internal/store/cases.go: CreateBump, LoadBump, UpdateBump applying resolution-style Changes in one transaction under the bumps row lock.

Both are recorded next to their tables in the contracts DDL.

title: design: triage dependabot pull requests
description: autophage's domain is issues only. internal/github/translate.go handles IssuesEvent, InstallationEvent and InstallationRepositoriesEvent and nothing else, and the App is not subscribed to pull_request at all (runbook step 4). resolution.Case is keyed by (repository, issue number), Branch() is autophage/<number>, and the attempt flow is clone default branch, cut a new branch, work, push, open a PR. A dependabot PR inverts all of that: the branch and the diff already exist, and the work is deciding whether the bump is safe and making CI green, not writing a fix from a description. OutcomeKind has no vocabulary for it either; pull_request_opened is the only success today.
design: Not a toggle on the issue path. Smallest honest version is judgement, not repair: subscribe to pull_request, run the repo's own tests in the existing sandbox against the PR head, post the result through the comment outbox, and let the existing approved label gate anything that writes. That reuses the sandbox, the budget tiers, the trust gate and the outbox, and invents no new write path. Repairing a red dependabot PR (pushing a fix commit onto someone else's branch) is a separate and much larger decision. Note dependabot's author_association is NONE, so the existing trust gate already routes it to Gated, which is the right default. Volume matters: 191 repositories are enrolled and dispatcher concurrency is 2.
acceptance_criteria: A DDD session produces the bounded context, the events, the outcome vocabulary and the contracts before any code.
close_reason: DDD session done. Bounded context, events, outcome vocabulary and contracts landed: docs/specs/2026-09-17-autophage-upkeep-domain-model.md, docs/specs/2026-09-17-autophage-upkeep-contracts.md, docs/adr/0007-dependabot-bumps-as-an-upkeep-context.md, plus the Upkeep rows in the context map. The filed design (run the repo tests in the sandbox and comment a verdict) was rejected: Actions already ran them and pushes the conclusion, so autophage consumes the rollup instead. Scope settled with Guy as repair the red ones, never merge, dependabot trusted by identity, per-repo opt-in. Implementation: autophage-auq, br4, d9r, n4o, a51, qe6.

title: an attempt branches from a stale default branch when an earlier autophage PR is unmerged
description: Reproduced live on guygrigsby/guygrigsby. Case #2 opened PR #3 changing README.md line 3 (HashiCorp -> Tailscale). Case #4 later opened PR #5 rewriting the same file, branched from master, which still said HashiCorp because #3 was unmerged. PR #5 therefore reasserts HashiCorp in both its intro and its new Work section, and the two diffs overlap textually. internal/agent/runner.go:349 and :543 always branch from and target repo.DefaultBranch, and nothing anywhere queries GitHub for other open autophage branches or PRs. Two cases on one repo can silently undo each other.
design: Options: have the brief name other open autophage PRs touching the repo so the agent can account for them; refuse or defer a case whose repo already has an open autophage PR; or branch from the newest open autophage branch rather than the default branch. Needs a decision before autophage runs on any repo with real issue volume.
acceptance_criteria: Two cases open on the same repo at once cannot produce PRs that contradict each other without the second attempt at least being told the first exists.
notes: Not a concurrency bug, and queueing or worktrees do not fix it. The two colliding attempts never overlapped: case #2 finished and its PR sat unmerged for about fifteen hours before case #4 started, and attempts_running never exceeded 1. The collision came from runner.go:349 and :543 branching from and targeting repo.DefaultBranch, which was stale because PR #3 had not merged. Serialising the cases would have produced the same two contradicting diffs. Only knowing about the open autophage PR fixes it.

title: sandbox: disk quotas for workspaces and cache volumes, cache discard after a hostile attempt
description: Plan D final review, Important 7: memory, cpu and pids are bounded; disk is not. A looping agent can fill the deploy host's disk from bash and take Postgres down with it, and /cache/go holds GOCACHE which the next attempt on the repository executes. Add a quota (xfs project quota or a sized volume) on the workspaces dir and the per-repository volumes, and a documented policy for discarding a repository's caches after a failed or hostile attempt.

title: sandbox: egress allowlist for the networked prep container
description: Plan D final review, Important 6: a lockfile committed by one attempt makes the next attempt's networked prep container fetch from attacker-chosen hosts (go direct VCS, npm resolved URLs, uv lock urls). Go is narrowed (proxy only, -mod=readonly). Add an egress allowlist (proxy.golang.org, registry.npmjs.org, pypi.org and files.pythonhosted.org) for the prep container, via a podman network with nftables rules or a forward proxy.

title: upkeep: bump and watch endpoints, CLI, status and metrics
description: The API rows in docs/specs/2026-09-17-autophage-upkeep-contracts.md: GET /api/bumps, GET /api/bumps/{owner}/{repo}/{number}, POST /api/bumps/.../retry, GET and POST /api/repairs/{id} and /stop, GET /api/repairs/{id}/why, PUT and DELETE /api/repositories/{owner}/{repo}/watch. GET /api/status and /metrics gain the bump series. CLI verbs to match the existing run, stop, status, why.
design: retry is the only escape hatch from sticky abandonment and the second place in the system that deletes a fact row rather than appending one. Starting a round is deliberately not an endpoint: the scheduler owns the queue, as it does for issue attempts.
acceptance_criteria: The operator can watch a repository, see a bump go red then green, and read the ledger for the round that fixed it, all through the CLI.

title: a merged pull request records the issue close as a rejected delivery
description: Observed live. Merging guygrigsby/guygrigsby#3 closed issue #2. The issues.closed delivery reached Case.Close on a case already in done, and case.go:357 refuses because Terminal() covers Done and Closed. internal/github/translate.go:91 maps ErrRefused to a rejected processing row, so the metric now reads deliveries_total{event="issues",result="rejected"} 1. Nothing breaks and the row is terminal, but the single most normal end to a case, someone merging the PR autophage opened, is recorded in the delivery ledger as a rejection.
design: Cheapest fix keeps Done terminal and stops calling the outcome a rejection: in the closed branch of Translator.issue, treat a refusal on an already-terminal case as ignored rather than rejected. Close today has exactly two failure modes, an empty delivery id (Invalid) and a terminal state (Refused), so errors.Is(err, resolution.ErrRefused) there is unambiguous, though a named sentinel would age better. The alternative, allowing Done to move to Closed, buys nothing: the done fact would survive only in the transition log.
acceptance_criteria: Merging an autophage PR leaves no rejected row in the delivery ledger.

description: EnqueueTriageComment and EnqueueOutcomeComment check-then-insert; two sweeps racing is untested.

title: store: cover AssignID refusals and sub-second intervals
description: AssignID's empty and already-assigned refusals are untested, and no test round-trips a sub-second INTERVAL.

title: store: Listen backoff never resets after a healthy stretch
description: A long-lived connection that later drops resumes at the last backoff instead of starting over.

title: store: RemoveRepository notifies for an unknown repository
description: The insert-select writes nothing when the repository is unknown but the notify fires anyway, waking a pointless sweep.

title: resolution: Outcome.cause CauseClosed fallback is unreachable
description: The final return in cause() cannot be hit now that RecordOutcome validates the reason first; drop it or prove it.

title: resolution: BuildBrief does not validate Repository
description: BuildBrief takes a zero Repository without complaint, and OwnerName trusts FullName has a slash.

title: resolution: cover target() attempt id mismatch
description: RecordRun and RecordOutcome refuse an attemptID that is not the open attempt; no test names that path.

title: resolution: cache Parse<Name> candidate slices
description: Every ParseX call rebuilds its candidate slice; hoist each to a package-level var.

title: agent/app: prune stale triage backoff entries; strip the URL form of closing keywords
description: Plan E final re-review residual minors: (1) internal/app/triage.go deletes a case's in-memory failure entry only after a successful RecordTriage; a case closed or whose repository was removed keeps its entry until restart (slow leak, one CaseKey each). Prune entries for cases no longer in ReceivedWithoutTriage each sweep. (2) internal/agent/runner.go stripClosingKeywords matches #n and owner/repo#n only; GitHub also closes on fixes https://github.com/owner/repo/issues/n, and a keyword and reference split across a newline is not matched.

title: daemon: BotEmail should carry the App user id; e2e does not cover the comment poster
description: Plan E final review minors 6 and 8: cmd/autophaged/main.go sets BotEmail to autophage[bot]@users.noreply.github.com; GitHub's convention is <app-user-id>+autophage[bot]@users.noreply.github.com so commits attribute to the App (the id is known only after registration; read it from the App's user via the API at boot or make it config). The e2e's happy path posts no comment, so the outbox poster is unproven end to end; add an exhausted-budget e2e variant.
